physicalNotes: Radius: the mean limb-darkened diameter of 3.143 +/- 0.027 mas that Evans et al. (2024, ApJ 971, 190) measure on Polaris Aa with CHARA/MIRC-X, at their adopted distance of 136.90 pc: 32,184,239 km, 46.26 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (the paper gives 46.27 +/- 0.42). GM from their dynamical mass of Polaris Aa, 5.13 +/- 0.28 solar masses, times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: no rotation axis is measured, so the presentation frame puts the display axis (celestial north at the star) up; the camera orbit then lies in the star's equator and reaches the Earth-facing hemisphere.

sources.position: SIMBAD basic record for * alf UMi (HD 8890, HIP 11767), ICRS J2000 position from the Hipparcos new reduction (van Leeuwen 2007, A&A 474, 653; bibcode 2007A&A...474..653V), retrieved 2026-09-16; cross-identification HIP 11767: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=HIP%2011767
sources.distance: 136.90 +/- 0.34 pc, the distance Evans et al. (2024, ApJ 971, 190) adopt: the Gaia DR3 parallax of the wide companion Polaris B (7.2869 +/- 0.0178 mas via SIMBAD) with the Lindegren zero-point offset. Polaris Aa itself is too bright for a reliable Gaia parallax; Hipparcos gives 7.54 mas (133 pc).
sources.properMotion: Hipparcos new reduction (van Leeuwen 2007) via SIMBAD: 44.48, -11.85 mas/yr
sources.radialVelocity: -16.42 km/s, the systemic velocity of the spectroscopic binary in the SB9 catalogue (Pourbaix et al. 2004, A&A 424, 727) via SIMBAD
